propositions: The snapshot janitor's free-space trigger uses an absolute 2 GiB floor that is disk-size-blind, requiring 93.3% used on a 30-GiB root to engage, which exceeds the 85% alarm threshold and the observed 90% peak.

Root disk usage climbed to 90% because every review materializes a fresh ~620 MiB copy of the 69,984-file ticket tree on a key advancing every ~26 seconds with negligible reuse, generating ~4.4 GiB/h of store growth in the container writable layer.
The janitor's 7-day cold-trim trigger is unreachable on a container recreated every few hours, and the byte-total backstop promised by the ADR and module docstring is not implemented in _gc_pass.
The fix adds a volume-relative watermark term so the reclaim trigger engages before the alarm floor on small volumes, with a fixed 5% hysteresis margin to prevent re-firing every interval.

Configuration of the new free_watermark_pct knob defaults to 0 (off) for backward compatibility and is set to 20 on the review-bot service via environment variable, clamped to a maximum of 50 to prevent pathological behavior.
